The constraint we start with

What slows professional services teams down.

We begin with the moments where people wait, repeat work, or lose context. Then we automate the predictable part and keep judgment with the right person.

01

Intake runs on inboxes and memory

Enquiries arrive by email, WhatsApp, calls and referrals. Details are re-typed into spreadsheets, conflict and acceptance checks depend on who remembers past matters, and work is either lost or accepted without the right checks.

02

Drafts start from the last client's file

Proposals, engagement letters, notices and reports are rebuilt from old documents each time. Partners lose evenings to formatting, wording drifts from the firm's standard, and a name or term copied from another client's matter becomes a confidentiality problem.

03

Clients are chased for the same documents every season

ITR, GST and audit seasons, court filings and campaign launches all stall on missing inputs. Staff send the same reminders by hand from personal phones and track replies in chat threads nobody else can see.

04

Deadlines live in diaries, not systems

Hearing dates, statutory due dates, notice response dates and client milestones sit in individual calendars and clerks' registers. When someone is on leave, the firm finds out about a missed date too late.

05

Time and fees leak quietly

Timesheets are filled at month end from memory, unbilled work waits for weeks, and fee reminders depend on an awkward personal call. Partners rarely have a current view of utilization, realization and pipeline.

06

Confidentiality limits which tools you can use

Client files, privileged communications and unpublished financials cannot be pasted into consumer AI tools. Firms need automation that respects matter-level access, professional conduct rules and the DPDP Act from the first design.

The perfect automation

From first enquiry to a signed, checked and onboarded engagement

One connected workflow takes a new enquiry from any channel, captures it once, runs the firm's conflict, independence or KYC checks, drafts the proposal or engagement letter from approved templates, and opens the matter or project with document requests the moment the client signs. Nothing is sent, accepted or priced until the responsible partner approves it.

  1. 01

    Capture the enquiry once

    Website forms, WhatsApp messages from people who contacted the firm, referral emails and front-desk calls become one intake record in the CRM with source, service line and consent. Existing clients are matched so nobody is entered twice.

    TTypeformWBWhatsApp Business PlatformHHubSpotnn8n
  2. 02

    Summarize and route to the right partner

    An AI step summarizes the request, suggests the practice area and urgency, and lists missing facts. Written rules route it to a named partner or account lead, and a response clock is visible to the team in Slack.

    ACAnthropic Claudenn8nSSlack
  3. 03

    Run conflict, independence and KYC checks

    Client, group company, director and opposing party names are searched against past clients and matters. CA firms add independence checks for audit clients and KYC where PMLA-specified activities are involved. Possible matches are listed with the reason each surfaced.

    SSupabasePPythonRRetool
  4. 04

    Draft the proposal or engagement letter

    The approved template for the engagement type is filled from the intake record and rate card. Agencies and consultancies get AI-drafted narrative sections from their own proposal library; law and CA firms get wording only from approved clauses.

    ACAnthropic ClaudeLLlamaIndexQQdrantNNotion
  5. 05

    Sign, open and onboard

    After e-signature, the workflow issues the matter or project number, sets up the team and task board, and sends the client a checklist with a secure upload link and named contacts by email or an approved WhatsApp template.

Human checkpoint

The responsible partner decides whether to accept the client after reviewing every conflict, independence or KYC flag, and approves scope, fee and the final letter or proposal before it is sent. The system never clears a conflict or sends a fee quote on its own.

What changes

  • Prompt, consistent replies to people who contact the firm, without any promotional outreach
  • Conflict and acceptance decisions recorded with reasons for every new client and matter
  • Proposals and engagement letters that start from approved wording, not another client's file
  • New clients onboarded with clear document requests and named contacts from the first day

Automation playbook

Start where the work repeats.

A selection from the playbook. Each blueprint shows the trigger, steps, tools, human checkpoint, data handling, deliverables, and measures.

Enquiry and first response · 2–3 weeks

Enquiry capture, qualification and routing

Every new enquiry from forms, email, WhatsApp or referrals becomes one CRM record with a short AI summary, a suggested service line and a named owner, so prospects get a prompt and relevant reply.

View the blueprint ↗Conflict, independence and KYC checks · 5–8 weeks

Client acceptance: conflicts, independence and KYC

New clients and matters are checked against the firm's own records for conflicts, auditor independence and, where the law requires it, client due diligence, with every possible match and decision recorded before work starts.

View the blueprint ↗Proposal and engagement terms · 4–6 weeks

Proposals and engagement letters from approved libraries

Proposals, statements of work and engagement letters start from the firm's approved templates and rate card. AI drafts narrative sections only where the firm allows it, and a partner edits and approves every document before it goes for signature.

View the blueprint ↗Onboarding and information gathering · 2–3 weeks

Agency client onboarding: access, brief and kick-off

When a statement of work is signed, the client gets one checklist for platform access, brand assets and the brief, and the team gets a ready project board, a shared channel and a kick-off agenda.

View the blueprint ↗Onboarding and information gathering · 4–6 weeks

Season-ready client document collection

For ITR, GST and audit work, each client gets a personalized checklist and a secure upload link, reminders follow an agreed schedule, and staff see in one tracker what is in, what is missing and what is ready for review.

View the blueprint ↗Dates, status and client updates · 4–5 weeks

Client compliance calendar and tax notice tracker

One calendar holds every client's GST, TDS, advance tax, income tax and ROC due dates, plus any notices received, so staff get assigned tasks and clients get reminders for the services they have engaged.

How we work

A clear delivery rhythm, from discovery to daily operation.

Five phases with named deliverables, client inputs, and review points. Most teams start with a focused pilot.

  1. 01 · 1–2 weeksDiscover

    We map how work actually moves through the firm, from intake and acceptance to engagement terms, onboarding, delivery, deadlines and billing. We meet partners, managers and the people who chase clients, and record the professional rules that shape the design, from Bar Council and ICAI limits to PMLA duties and DPDP obligations.

  2. 02 · 1–2 weeksDesign

    We design each chosen workflow step by step: triggers, data fields, templates, message wording, decision points and the named person at every checkpoint. Client-facing wording, consent text and acceptance rules are reviewed by the firm's risk or compliance partner before anything is built.

  3. 03 · 2–6 weeksBuild

    We configure and build in the firm's own accounts wherever possible: n8n workflows, CRM and project tool setup, secure upload stores, retrieval indexes and dashboards. Templates and knowledge sources are loaded with named owners, and every AI step logs its inputs, outputs and sources.

  4. 04 · 1–2 weeksValidate & launch

    We test on real but limited cases, including the awkward ones: duplicate clients, near-miss conflict names, wrong documents, missed dates and questions the assistant should decline. Partners review outputs before launch, and staff are trained on what the system does and what remains their decision.

  5. 05 · Ongoing, reviewed monthlyOperate & improve

    After launch we monitor runs, failures and exceptions, review a sample of AI outputs with the knowledge or risk owner, update templates and calendars when laws, forms or due dates change, and add the next workflow once the first is stable.

Suggested first pilot

A four-week pilot: one practice, one workflow, measured

We start with one workflow in one team where the pain is clear and the data is reachable: season document collection in a CA firm, the hearing diary for a litigation team, or onboarding and status reports for a set of agency or consulting clients. The pilot runs on real work with a small group, and the measures and the continue-or-stop decision are agreed before it starts.

  • One workflow, one practice or team, and a defined set of clients or matters
  • Integration with only the systems that workflow needs, in the firm's own accounts
  • Templates and client message wording approved by the responsible partner
  • Baseline and pilot-period measures agreed in writing
  • An end-of-pilot review with a recommendation to extend, change or stop

Measures

Know whether it is working.

Proposed measures, agreed with your team before launch, with a source, owner, and review cadence.

First meaningful response time

Elapsed working time from a valid enquiry arriving to a relevant reply from a person, or an approved acknowledgement with clear next steps.

Time to acceptance decision

Working days from a complete intake form to a recorded conflict, independence or KYC decision by the responsible partner.

Proposal or engagement turnaround

Working days from a scoping call or cleared intake to the proposal, statement of work or engagement letter being sent.

Document completeness by cut-off

Share of clients whose required documents are received and verified by the firm's internal cut-off date for the season.
